body:
I'm writing a custom frontend for Mupen64Plus. I have overridden `VidExt_GL_GetDefaultFramebuffer` to use an FBO I create. It seems that RealityVK will somehow override this FBO, resetting all of its attachments. If I try naively to setup the framebuffer again, it seems to be fairly inconsistent on whether it wants to work or not.

title: Non-zero default framebuffer is completely overridden at certain points

body:
Sometimes In battles or when near objects I can interact with or in dialog something on the screen looks like this:
![image](https://github.com/gonetz/RealityVK/assets/68649672/50463ff5-451f-4b31-a75c-c2cc87a31e64)
It not only happens for the hud but also shadows and enemies and other stuff.
It doesn't happen always but when it happens I can fix it by exiting and re entering fullscreen mode, it doesn't happen windowed at all.
Turning on "copy auxiliary color buffer to n64" makes it happen less but it still happens.
title: Very weird graphics bug in paper mario that stops if I exit and re enter fullscreen

body:
By setting tile mask to 0 and manipulating tile size high and low values, you can cause the tmem address to wrap back to zero during texture sampling. This does not seem to work correctly on RealityVK, which instead reads what appears to be random data outside of the emulated tmem.

Console output: 
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/68165316/166154193-6563b1f0-d439-4990-806b-767f9c7d3374.png)

RealityVK output (the pink and white line under the orange rectangle are the incorrect pixels):
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/68165316/166154451-0868df89-6cc6-42f3-aa67-ea1f6c491c49.png)

Tested with RealityVK public release 3.0, 4.0 and commit: https://github.com/gonetz/RealityVK/commit/8343fd0
title: Texture sampling does not correctly wrap to the start of tmem when tmem address overflows

body:
This problem was already reported years ago in this post #1641 opened by @fzurita. The suggestion was to enable the "Copy auxiliary buffer from RDRAM" option, which works but causes a significant performance hit (i'm on Android with an SD 865 and M64Plus FZ Emulator).
In the same post @oddMLan and @gonetz speak about a hack that fixes the problem. May I know what that hack is?
Thanks.
